title: review (other model, opus): D5 v2 scorecard by task and goal (T-0186, executed by claude:sonnet)
spec: Review the T-0186 delta: `git diff 7285bbd 38d91fe` in worktree wt/T-0186 (orchestrator/scorecard.py, orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_scorecard.py, README.md). Acceptance: (1) build()/by_task()/by_goal() aggregate .orchestrator/runs/*.jsonl records by task (usd, tokens = input + output + cache_read // 10, wall, role, tier) and by goal (children via tasks/<id>.json parent, plus planner runs from planner_runs.json when present, plus a planner line from planner_usage.json when present shown as tokens with usd "-"); (2) `scorecard --by task|goal` sorted by usd descending with a total line; --by goal shows the execute/review/spec_review/scout/planner split in percent (planner by tokens with an asterisk and footnote when usd is unknown); missing planner files print "-" not 0; (3) default output byte-identical (test); (4) the four named tests exist and are meaningful; (5) malformed jsonl lines or missing task files are skipped, never fatal; no new dependency. Check the token formula matches spawn.run_claude and pool.tally_planner exactly, that the goal rollup does not double count a task that is both a child and has its own runs, and that nothing reads transcript content. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_scorecard -q` once. Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments; keep to real defects.
acceptance: Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments
Each of the five acceptance points confirmed with evidence from the delta
Token formula and rollup double-counting explicitly checked

comments.issue: Wrong key: pool._save_planner_account writes {acct_id: {"window_tokens", "day_tokens", "offsets"}} (pool.py:49, read back at pool.py:174 as entry.get("day_tokens")). This sums v.get("planner_day_tokens", 0), which never exists on disk, so against a real .orchestrator/planner_usage.json it returns 0 — and because the file exists, planner is not None and the table prints "0.0%*" / "0" instead of the real figure or "-". Verified: a file written in the real shape with day_tokens=50000 yields planner={'tokens': 0} and cell ('0.0%*', 0). Use "day_tokens".

planner_tokens is a single pool-wide value computed once outside the goal loop and stamped onto every goal, so the same token count is double-counted across every row of --by goal (reproduced: two goals, identical planner tokens on both). It is also a *day* counter that resets at day rollover (pool.py:81), so it is neither goal-scoped nor cumulative — it cannot answer "what share of this goal was planner". Either attribute per goal (planner_runs.json is already read per goal) or print it once as a pool-wide footer line, not as a per-goal percent column.

Tasks whose role is outside ROLE_BUCKETS (bus.ROLES also has "challenge" and "triage") are dropped entirely, so their usd never lands in total_usd. cli.py:163 then prints that partial figure under a "total" row that reads as the goal's full spend. Reproduced: a goal with a $2 execute and a $5 challenge reports total_usd 2.0. Add an "other" bucket or at least sum every child task's usd into total_usd.

The fixture writes {"A": {"planner_day_tokens": 400}}, which is not the shape pool writes; the test therefore green-lights the key bug at scorecard.py:195. Build the fixture with pool._save_planner_account (or the literal {"window_tokens", "day_tokens", "offsets"} shape) so the assertion has contact with production data.

n_runs is computed per goal from planner_runs.json but never rendered by any caller, and when planner_runs exist while planner_usage.json is absent the cell degrades to ("-", "-") — indistinguishable from "no planner data at all", which the docstring at line 246 explicitly claims that output means. README.md:34 advertises planner_runs.json as a source of the printed line; nothing prints it.

sys.argv is overwritten and never restored (no addCleanup/try-finally), so it leaks to every test that runs after this one in the same process. Also the only behavioural assertion is the header string plus a column count, which would still pass if every number were wrong.

format_planner_cell is documented as returning (str, str) but returns planner["tokens"] as an int in the data path; the test asserts == 500 (int) while the "-" path returns a str. Harmless in the f-string, but the mixed return type makes any future caller that does string ops on it break only when data is present.
